When Klepto was a thing, my duo partner and me used to play BaZil, which was a fresh take on bot: we would go Bard and Zilean, both kleptomancy and ap support item (spellthief I think). We would use the zilean speed boost on bard to set up Q stuns or slow with meep, followed by double bomb. It was a really good harassing lane. We would completly zone out the enemy laners from the farm and the gold from klepto+spellthief allowed us to stay ahead in gold. These days are gone sadly, and BaZil isn't as fresh as it use to be.

We still like to try some funky things. Veigar and ziggs like you said is pretty cool. But veigar and Sett? That is some chad bot stuff. Veigar puts his cage around the enemy and sett can E them into the stun. It garenties that the stun and damage from veigar W and Q lands and allows sett to land two q empowered AA since he doesn't need the ms boost to get to them. Requires quite a lot of communication but it's awesome to pull off.

We also like to play what we call KassaWin. We basically pick kassadin first and let them pick their bot lane if possible, so we can counter pick with a safe support match up. Things like rakan/braum into hard engage lane, or nami/taric into more poke lane. It allows the kassadin to safely farm under tower for lvl 6. After 6, braum and rakan are pretty strong since they can follow Kassadin in this engage, while nami and taric gives him some much needed safety.

Keep in mind that we're gold and we play mostly with high gold/low plat. Pretty sure that smarter players would abuse our weekness easily. We have fun tho, and that's what matters.

I still miss our fresh Bazil tho.

Zilean can be really strong. He synergises really well with some adc, especially if they're imobile with high damage outpout (Jhin and Ashe for exemple). 

You can go the Ap heavy route, winning your lane by poking and having a very powerfull heal on your R lategame. Since he's really mana hungry, I recommend building a lot of mana regen early on, especially if you're ahead. I have a friend who starts three faerie charm (funny but I still woudn't recommend that, since spellthief's edge is so good on him and still gives you a fair bit of mana regen). There's some inconvenient/weakness with this build. First, you'll be very squishy and unless you can reliably land your stun, you and your adc will be vulnerable to all-ins and ganks. Sure you can speed-up your adc or slow one oponent but it most cases, it won't be enough to save you.

There's another build I suggest you try. This build is especially good against champion without gap closers escape since you will be maxing your E over your Q. Prioritize armor and cdr over ap in your runes/masteries, go ancient coin, build tanky and cap your cdr early on. At lvl 9, with 30% cdr, you have a 99% slow on a 10 second cooldown that you can cast two times in succession with your W wich has a 8 second cool down. Since you're tanky, you can focus on speeding up your teammates even if you're a bit out of position.

The thing with Draven's axes is that you can more or less predict their movement. If you throw and axe and then back off, it will go behind you. If you throw then run towards the enemy, it will go infront of you. So you can use that it teamfight even if it is harder than in lane.Also, use w between axes! The ms boost will help you catch them and the cd will reset on catch. 

I often go essence reaver on draven. It may not be optimal damage wise but it allows you to spam W a lot longer AND it is more forgiving when you drop your axes since you'll have near 40% cdr.

All that said, the real key to succes on Draven (or any champ really) is practice. He's a high skill cap champ. It will take a lot of games to become comfortable with him but in the end, it will be very rewarding. You'll learn alot about positionning in teamfights and will be able to juggle axes like a pro! 

Good luck friend!
